_about: US amateur transmit privileges by operator class. THIS FILE HAS LEGAL WEIGHT.
It is a transcription of the regulation, not a summary of it. The two CFR
tables are carried separately, exactly as they appear in the source, and the
join that produces 'may this class send this mode here' is done in code with
tests (CLAUDE.md 0: generate, do not transcribe twice). A pre-joined table
would be a third artefact that could disagree with both its parents.
Every row cites the paragraph it came from. Figures that could not be
sourced are in 'unknowns' with a reason, never guessed (CLAUDE.md 4).
Region 2 columns only. Hamlet is a US application; Regions 1 and 3 are
listed as an explicit unknown rather than half-copied.

sources.note: NOT the authority. The ARRL chart is a rendering of the sections above and is widely recognized, so it is named here as the familiar picture this data should agree with. Where the chart and the CFR ever differ, the CFR wins and this file follows the CFR.

rules.text: Except as specified elsewhere in this part, an amateur station may transmit a CW emission on any frequency authorized to the control operator.
rules._note: This is why the emission table below does not list CW: CW follows the class frequency table alone.

rules.text: A station having a control operator holding a Novice or Technician Class operator license may only transmit a CW emission using the international Morse code.

A station having a control operator holding a Novice Class operator license or a Technician Class operator license may only transmit a CW emission using the international Morse code or phone emissions J3E and R3E.

Phone and image emissions may be transmitted only by stations located in ITU Regions 1 and 3, and by stations located within ITU Region 2 that are west of 130 degrees West longitude or south of 20 degrees North latitude.
rules._note: Excludes the contiguous United States. Applied conservatively: unless the operator's grid square proves they qualify, a segment carrying this standard is treated as not available to them, and the status line says which rule did it.

classFrequencyBands._note: Which frequencies each class may transmit on at all, before emission type is considered. Novice and Technician share one table in 97.301(e).

Technician._note: 97.301(e) covers Novice and Technician together. HF only below; VHF/UHF privileges exist and are listed as an unknown, since Hamlet is HF-only in phase 1.

Novice._note: Identical to Technician: the regulation gives them one table.

emissionRanges._note: Where each emission type other than CW may be sent, regardless of class. CW is absent on purpose: 97.305(a) allows it on any frequency authorized to the control operator.

upgradePaths._note: Editorial, not regulation: what the next license buys, for the 'what would General unlock?' panel. The frequencies it quotes come from the tables above rather than from this text.

unknowns.reason: 60 m is five discrete channels with their own rules (97.303(h), 97.305(c)(3)(iii), 97.307(f)(14)), not a contiguous segment like every other HF band. Hamlet's band plan does not include 60 m, so encoding it here would add a shape the rest of the code cannot represent. Must be added before 60 m appears in BandPlan.

97.301(a) and (e) grant VHF/UHF privileges that are real and not transcribed here. Hamlet is HF-only through phase 4; a Technician's 2 m privileges are their most-used privilege and this file would mislead if read as complete. Must be added before any VHF band appears.
97.301 lists all three regions; only Region 2 is transcribed. Hamlet is a US application and a half-copied foreign table is worse than an absent one.
97.313 sets power limits, including per-band and per-class ones. Not needed for a transmit-privilege overlay and not transcribed. Must be added before Hamlet says anything about power.
97.221 automatic-control segments and the 97.307(f) bandwidth standards are not encoded. Hamlet does not yet claim anything about either.
